name: Health coverage if you're pregnant
whatYouGet: Explains that all Marketplace and Medicaid plans cover pregnancy and childbirth, and how to apply (create an account for Marketplace coverage, or check Medicaid/CHIP eligibility) or report a pregnancy or birth.
costDetail: Free to apply; Medicaid/CHIP coverage is free or low-cost; Marketplace plans may have premiums.
eligibility: People who are pregnant or recently gave birth; Medicaid/CHIP depends on state and income.
catches: Pregnancy alone does not open a Special Enrollment Period; the birth of a child does (apply within 60 days of birth). Open Enrollment runs Nov 1 - Jan 15. Marketplace plans can have premiums, deductibles and copays.
notes: Medicaid or CHIP coverage can begin any time if you are eligible.
valueBasis: HHS (ASPE) 2010-11 payments for a birth episode: about $9,100 to $13,600 Medicaid, $18,300 to $27,900 commercial; old data, not a current price
whenNote: Pregnancy alone does not open a Special Enrollment Period; Open Enrollment runs Nov 1 to Jan 15; Medicaid/CHIP can start any time.

name: Medicaid & CHIP coverage (pregnancy)
whatYouGet: Free or low-cost coverage for eligible pregnant women; CHIP states can cover prenatal, delivery and postpartum care, and newborns of covered mothers are deemed eligible.
costDetail: Free or low-cost; varies by state
eligibility: Income-based (MAGI) and non-financial criteria; rules vary by state. Postpartum care is covered at least 60 days, and many states extend to 12 months.
catches: Details such as income limits differ by state.
notes: You can apply any time of year. When a pregnant woman is enrolled in Medicaid or CHIP, her newborn is automatically enrolled (InsureKidsNow.gov).
valueBasis: HHS (ASPE) 2010-11 Medicaid payments for a birth episode: about $9,100 (vaginal) to $13,600 (cesarean); old data, not a current price
whenNote: You can apply any time of year; postpartum coverage lasts at least 60 days and many states extend to 12 months.

name: TennCare diaper benefit
whatYouGet: Up to 100 diapers a month for TennCare and CoverKids members under age 2, picked up at a participating pharmacy.
costDetail: No cost or copay; no prescription needed.
eligibility: Babies under age 2 enrolled in TennCare or CoverKids; the baby is eligible only after birth.
catches: Limit of 100 diapers per 30 days and 200 per 60 days from an approved brand list. Only after the baby is born. Pharmacy must participate.
notes: Newborns waiting on an ID can use the parent's TennCare pharmacy ID. Update TennCare Connect after birth.
freeStuff: Free diapers from a participating pharmacy for TennCare or CoverKids babies.
valueBasis: Up to 100 newborn diapers a month at about $0.30 each, for 6 to 12 months
whenNote: The baby becomes eligible only after birth.

name: Delaware Medicaid postpartum diapers, wipes and meals
brand: Delaware Health and Social Services (Diamond State Health Plan)
whatYouGet: For 12 weeks after birth, Medicaid covers up to 80 diapers and a pack of wipes a week, plus home-delivered meals or a shelf-stable food box.
costDetail: Covered by Delaware Medicaid for postpartum members.
eligibility: Low-income postpartum members of the Diamond State Health Plan (Delaware Medicaid).
catches: This is a Medicaid waiver pilot; I found no 2026 page confirming it still runs. The state has warned of possible cuts. How to claim (through the Medicaid plan) is not spelled out in the results.
notes: Terms from the June 2024 state announcement and the waiver page.
freeStuff: Free diapers, wipes and meals for 12 weeks after birth for Delaware Medicaid members.
valueBasis: 80 diapers a week for 12 weeks at about $0.30 plus 12 packs of wipes at about $3; meals not counted
whenNote: Benefit runs for the first 12 weeks after birth.

name: Aetna Better Health pregnancy rewards and baby items
whatYouGet: Medicaid members earn a gift card, or in Illinois a car seat, highchair or play yard, for prenatal visits; amounts depend on the state plan.
costDetail: Members of the plan only; earned by attending visits.
eligibility: Members of an Aetna Better Health Medicaid plan in the listed states.
catches: Only for members of that plan. Kentucky and Oklahoma need 7 prenatal visits and 37+ weeks; Illinois needs a health risk screening and a prenatal visit; Florida and Louisiana give a $150 or $50 baby-items stipend. Page dates vary.
notes: Amounts seen: KY up to $90, OK $100, FL $150, LA $50.
freeStuff: Gift card (or in Illinois a car seat, highchair or play yard) for plan members who keep prenatal visits.
whenNote: Kentucky and Oklahoma reward is earned at 37 weeks or later.

name: AmeriHealth Caritas Bright Start rewards
whatYouGet: Plan members who join Bright Start can earn CARE Card or gift card rewards, a breast pump, and a portable crib or car seat for prenatal visits.
eligibility: Pregnant members of AmeriHealth Caritas Delaware (reward list seen); Florida and Ohio pages describe care management without amounts.
region: DE (rewards listed); FL, OH care management
catches: Delaware figures come from pages up to a year old. Must enroll (1-833-669-7672) and complete visits (for example eight prenatal visits by 38 weeks for the crib or car seat). A 2027 page mentions changed extras.
notes: Delaware list: $15 for reporting pregnancy early, $30 for four visits by week 26, $30 postpartum visit.
freeStuff: Gift cards plus a portable crib or car seat for members who complete prenatal visits.
valueBasis: $15 + $30 + $30 in cards, plus a portable crib or car seat at about $80 to $100 at the high end
whenNote: Rewards are tied to visits by set weeks; enroll as early as possible.

name: CareSource Babies First rewards
whatYouGet: Medicaid members who enroll can earn rewards on a prepaid card for prenatal, postpartum and well-baby visits.
costDetail: Members of the plan only; must enroll each pregnancy.
eligibility: CareSource Medicaid members in states with the program (Indiana, Kentucky, Ohio and others).
catches: Rewards post only after the claim is processed (up to 45 to 60 days). Amounts differ by state and some brochures are old.
notes: Seen: Indiana up to $200, Kentucky up to $150, Ohio $75 for the first prenatal visit.
freeStuff: Prepaid-card rewards for prenatal, postpartum and well-baby visits.
valueBasis: Plan materials say Ohio $75 first visit, Kentucky up to $150, Indiana up to $200
whenNote: Re-enroll with each pregnancy; earn from early prenatal visits.

name: My Health Pays prenatal rewards (Centene Medicaid plans)
brand: Sunshine Health, Superior HealthPlan, Coordinated Care, Peach State Health Plan
whatYouGet: Medicaid members earn money on a prepaid card for early prenatal visits and a postpartum visit.
eligibility: Medicaid or CHIP members of the listed plans.
catches: Superior requires enrollment from Jan 1, 2027 and caps rewards at $150 a year; Coordinated Care 2027 requires a Notification of Pregnancy. Amounts differ by plan and year.
notes: Superior TX $75 to $100 first-trimester visit; Sunshine FL up to $100; Coordinated WA $25 (2026) rising to $30; Peach State GA up to $90 for pregnancy items.
freeStuff: Prepaid-card rewards for early prenatal visits and a postpartum visit.
valueBasis: Plan pages state $25 to $100 per visit and a $150 yearly cap at Superior
whenNote: First-trimester visits (or within 42 days of enrolling) earn the most.

name: WellCare of North Carolina Better Beginnings rewards
whatYouGet: Medicaid members who notify the plan of pregnancy earn $25 for a prenatal visit and $25 for a postpartum visit, plus a choice of stroller, play yard, car seat or diapers.
eligibility: WellCare of NC Medicaid members who submit a Notification of Pregnancy.
catches: Must notify the plan before the birth. Up to $75 a year in rewards. A New Parent package and free pump are also mentioned; confirm with the plan.
notes: South Carolina and Georgia WellCare pages exist but are older and not included.
freeStuff: Rewards plus a stroller, play yard, car seat or diapers for members who attend a prenatal visit.
valueBasis: $25 to $50 in rewards plus one item such as a play yard at about $80 to $100
whenNote: Notify the plan during pregnancy; reward follows a prenatal visit.

name: Blue Cross Special Beginnings maternity rewards
brand: Blue Cross Community Health Plans (Illinois) and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas
whatYouGet: Medicaid members who join Special Beginnings can get a car seat or portable crib or gift cards for prenatal and postpartum visits.
eligibility: Pregnant members of Blue Cross Community Health Plans (IL) or BCBSTX Medicaid/CHIP; join by phone 1-888-421-7781.
catches: Sources disagree on exact rewards ($30 cards vs a car seat or crib in IL; $50 and $25 cards in TX). Enrolling is generally required.
notes: Plan name and Baby Yourself program not found in results.
freeStuff: A car seat or portable crib (Illinois) or gift cards (Texas) for plan members who enroll and attend visits.
valueBasis: Texas $50 + $25 cards, or an Illinois crib or car seat at about $80 to $100 plus a $30 card
whenNote: Join early in pregnancy; first-trimester visit earns the reward.

name: Highmark MOM Options and MOM Matters
brand: Highmark Health Options and Highmark Wholecare
whatYouGet: Medicaid members who keep prenatal visits can choose an infant car seat, stroller, Pack n Play or baby shower box; Wholecare pays money for visits and offers free classes and rides.
eligibility: Highmark Health Options (DE, WV) or Highmark Wholecare (PA) Medicaid members.
catches: Search summaries only; the exact amounts and visit rules were not shown.
notes: Highmark Baby Blocks not found. Baby Blueprints is a commercial-plan coaching program.
freeStuff: A choice of car seat, stroller or Pack n Play for plan members who keep prenatal visits.
valueBasis: One baby item such as a portable crib at about $80 to $100
whenNote: Rewards tied to regular prenatal visits.

name: Wellpoint Medicaid baby essentials gift card
whatYouGet: Washington members can get a $100 gift card for baby items, and West Virginia members up to $170 after six prenatal visits.
eligibility: Wellpoint Medicaid members in WA or WV who complete required visits.
catches: One card per pregnancy. Anthem Ohio offers a choice of two items; amounts on some Anthem pages are old.
notes: Healthy Rewards line seen: 888-990-8681.
freeStuff: A gift card for baby items for Wellpoint Medicaid members.
valueBasis: Plan pages state $100 (WA) and up to $170 (WV)
whenNote: Card is earned through prenatal visits.

name: UPMC for You Baby Steps baby gift
whatYouGet: Medicaid members who finish the Baby Steps program can pick a free baby gift bundle.
costDetail: Members of UPMC for You only.
eligibility: UPMC for You members who join Baby Steps before 34 weeks and start prenatal care before 13 weeks.
catches: Must join by 34 weeks, keep calls and prenatal tests. Gift format changed over the years (car seat, stroller, play yard, now an online bundle).
notes: Eligibility set by the Baby Steps health coach.
freeStuff: A baby gift bundle for members who complete Baby Steps.
valueBasis: One portable crib or car seat equivalent at about $80 to $100
whenNote: Join before 34 weeks of pregnancy.

name: Kaiser Permanente prenatal and childbirth classes
whatYouGet: Members can take childbirth preparation and newborn classes at no fee at most regions.
costDetail: No fee for members; one site lists $150 per couple for nonmembers.
eligibility: Kaiser Permanente members; some regions open some classes to nonmembers.
catches: Fees and formats differ by region; register 3 to 4 weeks ahead at some sites.
notes: Only for people with Kaiser coverage.
freeStuff: Free childbirth preparation classes for Kaiser members.
valueBasis: One site lists $150 per couple for nonmembers
whenNote: Classes are usually taken in the third trimester; register weeks ahead.

name: Pampers free online childbirth classes
whatYouGet: A free online series of childbirth classes led by clinical experts, from labor to postpartum care.
eligibility: Anyone expecting a baby.
catches: Pages are undated; one says 10 parts, another 9. Confirm that it is still offered.
freeStuff: Free online childbirth classes.
whenNote: Classes cover labor and birth, so most useful before the due date.

name: Aeroflow prenatal and breastfeeding classes
whatYouGet: Live classes on pregnancy, pumping and breastfeeding billed to your insurance as a preventive lactation benefit.
costDetail: Aeroflow says many plans cover them in full; some list a small copay or deductible.
eligibility: Members of plans that cover preventive lactation benefits.
catches: Aetna and TRICARE cap combined preventive lactation visits at 6 a year, so classes use up visits. Aeroflow pages conflict on cost-sharing.
notes: Backed by Aeroflow pages only, not by insurers.
freeStuff: Insurance-paid prenatal and breastfeeding classes.
whenNote: Aeroflow suggests 2 to 3 classes during pregnancy and saving the rest for after birth.

name: Aeroflow breast pump resupply through insurance
whatYouGet: Replacement pump parts and milk storage bags shipped on a schedule when your plan covers them, even if the pump came from elsewhere.
costDetail: Many plans cover in full; some have a small copay or deductible.
eligibility: Members of plans that cover pump supplies.
catches: Coverage varies by plan; some pages are old or show items out of stock. Babylist says many plans reimburse parts from 30 days after birth for up to a year.
notes: Babylist Health and Pumping Essentials only route pumps (Pumping Essentials works through Aeroflow), so not added.
freeStuff: Free replacement pump parts and milk storage bags through insurance.
whenNote: Resupply usually starts after the baby is born.

name: WIC Farmers Market Nutrition Program
whatYouGet: Coupons for fresh fruits, vegetables and herbs at approved farmers markets, issued on top of regular WIC benefits.
eligibility: WIC-certified women, infants over 4 months and children; offered only by participating states.
catches: Not every state or local agency runs it. Federal benefit is $10 to $30 a year; states may add more.
notes: Ask the local WIC office.
freeStuff: Farmers market produce coupons for WIC participants.
valueBasis: USDA says $10 to $30 a year per person federally
whenNote: Issued to certified WIC participants, including pregnant women.

name: WIC breastfeeding support and enhanced food package
whatYouGet: WIC breastfeeding mothers can get a peer counselor and an enhanced food package, and many WIC offices lend or give breast pumps.
eligibility: WIC participants who breastfeed; pump rules and peer counselor access vary by state.
catches: 63% of state agencies set conditions for a single-user electric pump; peer counselors are not available everywhere. Food amounts differ between two USDA pages.
notes: Extra to the usda-wic entry; fully breastfeeding mothers get more food for up to 12 months.
freeStuff: Extra WIC food, a peer counselor and often a breast pump for breastfeeding mothers.
whenNote: Fully breastfeeding mothers can keep the package until the baby is 12 months old.

name: Count the Kicks free app
whatYouGet: A free app and paper charts to count baby movements in the third trimester and spot changes early.
eligibility: Anyone pregnant; starting at 28 weeks (26 if high risk).
catches: Not medical advice; call your provider if movements change.
freeStuff: A free kick-counting app.
whenNote: Counting starts at 28 weeks, or 26 weeks for high-risk pregnancies.

name: Postpartum Support International online support groups
whatYouGet: Free weekly online support groups for pregnant and postpartum parents on Zoom, including first-time moms and loss support.
costDetail: Free; skip the paid upgrade offered at sign-up.
eligibility: Pregnant and postpartum people and partners.
catches: Groups cap at 16 to 25 people; arrive early. The helpline is a separate listed entry.
freeStuff: Free online peer support groups.
whenNote: Open during pregnancy and up to two years postpartum for the main group.

name: March of Dimes Mom & Baby Mobile Health Centers
whatYouGet: Mobile clinics giving prenatal and postpartum care, free or regardless of ability to pay, in selected communities.
costDetail: Free or pay-what-you-can at some sites; confirm per site.
eligibility: People in underserved areas, including the uninsured and underinsured.
region: Columbus and Southeast OH, Tucson and Phoenix AZ, DC area, New York City, Houston
catches: Limited locations. Whether every site is free was not confirmed.
notes: New centers planned in AZ and AL in 2026.
freeStuff: Prenatal and postpartum care in a mobile clinic.
whenNote: Prenatal care is best started early.

name: New York free portable crib
brand: New York State Department of Health
whatYouGet: Families with no safe place for baby to sleep may get a free portable crib and sheet through their local social services office.
eligibility: Households on public assistance or with limited resources.
catches: Apply through the local department of social services. Hospitals and home visiting programs also give safe sleep kits.
notes: Check CPSC recalls on any donated crib.
freeStuff: A free portable crib and sheet for families in need.
whenNote: Needed before the baby comes home.

name: Alabama Baby Box Initiative
whatYouGet: Expecting and new parents can pick up a free Baby Box with safe sleep education from a local DHR office.
eligibility: Expecting and new parents in Alabama.
catches: Pick up in person at the county DHR office; supplies may vary.
notes: Current stock not confirmed.
freeStuff: A free Baby Box (safe sleep space).
whenNote: Offered to expecting and new parents.

name: Virginia seat distribution program
whatYouGet: Free child car seats for families that qualify by income, given out at local sites.
eligibility: Parents eligible for WIC, SNAP, Medicaid, TANF or FAMIS with a child 7 or younger.
catches: Call 1-800-732-8333 to find a local site.
freeStuff: A free car seat for income-eligible Virginia families.
valueBasis: One infant car seat at about $100
whenNote: Get the seat before the hospital trip home.

name: Texas Safe Riders child safety seats
brand: Texas Department of State Health Services
whatYouGet: Free or low-cost car seats for low-income families after an education session.
eligibility: Low-income families or those with financial hardship; caregivers attend a class.
catches: Call 800-252-8255 for a site; seat supply depends on the site.
freeStuff: A free car seat for qualifying Texas families.
valueBasis: One infant car seat at about $100
whenNote: Get the seat before the baby is born.

name: Mississippi Safe Riders Magnolia
whatYouGet: Car seat distribution for low-income households applied for through an online form.
eligibility: Low-income households or those receiving federal aid.
catches: Details thinly shown; confirm with injuryprevention@msdh.ms.gov.
freeStuff: A car seat for qualifying Mississippi families.
valueBasis: One infant car seat at about $100
whenNote: Apply before the baby arrives.

name: Family Connects nurse home visit
whatYouGet: A free nurse home visit about 3 weeks after birth to check mother and baby and link families to help.
eligibility: All families with newborns in participating communities.
catches: Only in communities that run it. Oregon and New Jersey have statewide versions.
notes: Ask the birth hospital or health department.
freeStuff: A free nurse visit at home after birth.
whenNote: Visit usually about 3 weeks after birth.

name: Vaccines for Children program
whatYouGet: Free childhood vaccines, including RSV antibody nirsevimab, for children who are Medicaid-eligible, uninsured, underinsured or American Indian/Alaska Native.
costDetail: Vaccine is free; the office may charge a visit fee.
eligibility: Children 18 and under in the listed groups.
catches: Underinsured children only get it at community health centers; CHIP-only children do not qualify. Ask the doctor to confirm they take VFC.
freeStuff: Free childhood vaccines for eligible babies.
whenNote: Vaccines begin at birth and through childhood.

name: Free preventive care for women under the ACA
whatYouGet: Most plans cover contraception, breastfeeding support and supplies and folic acid at no cost, including after birth.
costDetail: No cost sharing when from an in-network provider.
eligibility: People with ACA-compliant plans; some religious employers are exempt.
catches: Pages are old. $0 is not guaranteed in every case. Tdap and flu in pregnancy and RSV were not confirmed here.
freeStuff: Contraception, lactation support and folic acid at no cost.
whenNote: Postpartum contraception and lactation support are used after birth.

name: MassHealth free prenatal vitamins
whatYouGet: MassHealth members can get prenatal vitamins free at a local pharmacy without a prescription.
eligibility: MassHealth members who are pregnant or lactating.
catches: Based on one search result from a provider page; confirm with the pharmacy.
freeStuff: Free prenatal vitamins from the pharmacy.
whenNote: Used during pregnancy.

name: Text4baby free text messages
whatYouGet: Three free texts a week with pregnancy and baby health tips, timed to the due date, until the baby turns one.
costDetail: Free, even without a text plan.
eligibility: Pregnant women and parents of babies under one.
catches: Undated pages; sponsor details differ, so confirm the service is still active.
notes: Text BABY (or BEBE) to 511411.
freeStuff: Free health text messages.
whenNote: Messages timed to the due date.
